text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.4% today to $127.53, continuing a broader slide over the past two weeks (-7.15%). The decline tracks with falling oil prices: US crude dropped to $96.41 per barrel after news that Iran has offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days and return to nuclear talks with the U.S. When geopolitical tensions ease and supply fears recede, oil becomes cheaper, which weighs on oil producers' earnings outlook and their stock prices.

The gap between US and global oil prices—US at $96, world at $115—suggests the market is pricing in relief from the conflict that has disrupted Middle Eastern shipping. Over the past week, ConocoPhillips has swung on each new headline about Iran negotiations or Houthi attacks, reflecting how directly crude producers depend on energy prices for their revenue.
